A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the magnification factor decreases with eccentricity, the size of the point image decreases from the fovea to the periphery and the number of retinal ganglion cells contributing to the representation of each point in V1 is similar throughout the visual field.
the visual topography in marmoset V1 is similar to that observed in larger monkeys, and that this topography is not affected by the shape of the cortical surface.
the magnification of the visual field is preserved across different species, and that it is independent of retinal ganglion cells density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in marmosets, the magnification factor decreases with eccentricity at the same rate as that reported in other primates, including humans.
the visual field map of V1 in marmosets is similar to that in macaque monkeys.
the relationship between cortical magnification factor and eccentricity is similar across species, including the small marmoset.
